newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nordic social democrats to hold Baltic Sea meeting.
newsitem.headline: Nordic social democrats to hold Baltic Sea meeting.

text.p: Nordic prime ministers said on Friday their ruling Social Democratic parties would organise an international meeting on Baltic Sea cooperation in April.

The meeting, which will draw Social Democratic leaders from Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, will be held in Mariehamn on the Finnish Baltic Sea island of Aaland on April 21-22, a statement said.

Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said the meeting would be a Social Democratic follow-up to an 11-nation Baltic Sea conference held in Visby on the Swedish Baltic Sea island of Gotland in June, 1996.

"The purpose is to form networks, promote cooperation, deepen integration -- to pursue a process that is so decisive for these four countries," he told a news conference after a two-day meeting of the Nordic Social Democratic parties outside Oslo.
Persson, who hosted the Visby conference, attended the meeting with fellow prime ministers Thorbjoern Jagland of Norway, Poul Nyrup Rasmussen and Paavo Lipponen of Finland.

The Visby declaration urged international finance institutions to step up participation in funding infrastructure and economic development in the Baltic Sea region. It also supported Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia and Poland in their bids to join the 15-nation European Union.
Denmark, Sweden and Finland are members of the EU while Norway, a non-member, has signed the European Economic Area cooperation agreement.
